card.name: Auxiliary verbs where 'develop' or 'occur' follows
card.fires_on: Small helper verbs such as 'may', 'was' or 'be' (and 'REACTIONS' split mid-word) right before a verb like occur, develop or be processed. It is most common in all-caps warning text.

modes.label: MAY in all-caps warnings
modes.description: The word MAY in capitalized warning text, just before a verb such as OCCUR or BE CONFUSED.
modes.example: CAUSE CROSS-HYPERSENSITIVITY AMONG BETA-LACTAM ANTIBACTERIAL DRUGS HAS BEEN CLEARLY DOCUMENTED AND<< MAY>> OCCUR IN UP TO 10

modes.label: Passive helper verbs in film text
modes.description: The helper verbs 'was' or 'be' in a passive clause about film being processed or recorded.
modes.example: After the film<< was>> processed, it was slit in half,

modes.label: Split word REACTIONS
modes.description: The ending of REACTIONS, split across pieces, before a phrase like ARE MORE LIKELY TO OCCUR.
modes.example: THESE REA<<CTIONS>> ARE MORE LIKELY TO OCCUR

card.writes: It pushes the model toward predicting 'develop' or 'development' as the next word.
card.plain: It fires on small helper words like 'may' where the next word is likely a verb such as 'develop' or 'occur'.
